messages:
ashok: heads-up — I found an unexpected access event. looks like a request routed through org-bridge-proxy allowed cross-org read on project `proj-884`.
ashok: snippet from audit (redacted):
```
2026-03-18T14:07:12Z service=org-bridge-proxy uid=svc-org-bridge-09 action=GET resource=projects/proj-884/policies result=200 actor_org=org-112 caller_org=org-998
```
ashok: caller_org != actor_org here. should not be possible with current isolation rules :rotating_light:

jordan: :eyes: can you paste the raw event id? want to trace through tenant-routing and envoy logs.
ashok: event id 94f3b2c7. pulled envoy logs — looks like proxy metrics show a policy-match on a legacy routing rule (route: allow-legacy-bridge)

elaine: that rule was supposed to be deprecated during the RBAC refactor last quarter. maybe the canary didn't remove it everywhere. i'll check the rollout history for org-bridge config.

sec-bot: ALERT: anomalous cross-org access detected for resource projects/proj-884. Rule matched: allow-legacy-bridge. Severity: high. Suggested action: revoke bridge SA keys, disable legacy route.

maria: immediate mitigation: rotate the service account used by org-bridge-proxy and add a short-lived deny-list on the proxy layer for caller_org=org-998. i'll put a temporary deny rule in front of the proxy routing table.
maria: repro command I used (safe, GET metadata only):
```
curl -H "X-Org: org-998" -H "Authorization: Bearer SVC_BRIDGE_TOKEN" https://proxy.internal/api/projects/proj-884/policies
```
maria: after rotate token, that same call returns 403.

ashok: ran an audit query across last 30 days — found 6 hits where caller_org != actor_org and route==allow-legacy-bridge. timestamps spread across two weeks.

jordan: ok — sounds like config drift during RBAC role/permission refactor. we need 2 tracks: (1) emergency mitigation (maria doing), (2) postmortem + fix and test matrix.

elaine: for the postmortem: let's check the rollout orchestration logs (deploy-tool) around the RBAC changes. possible the deletion of allow-legacy-bridge rule was gated behind a flag.

maria: raising a PR to remove the legacy route permanently and add an explicit test asserting actor_org==caller_org for project-scoped requests. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/org-bridge/+/PR-421
maria: PR includes unit test and e2e job that spins up two orgs and exercise cross-org calls.

devex-bot: Note: add alert rule to runtime-monitoring:metric("cross_org_access_count") > 0 -> pager to eng-security.

ashok: also verified KMS bindings. the org-bridge SA had decrypt rights on a shared key used for request-metadata — but that key is scoped to actor_org by policy. KMS audit shows decrypts from svc-org-bridge-09 while actor_org=org-112 — looks consistent with the proxy issue, not a KMS compromise.

jordan: action items:
- maria: rotate SA keys + deny rule (done)
- ashok: collect full list of impacted projects and export to spreadsheet
- elaine: audit rollout logs + find where allow-legacy-bridge persisted
- maria: follow up PR for removal + tests (PR-421)
- security: schedule 1hr postmortem sync tomorrow 10:00 PST

maria: quick note — I'm also going to add a canary that validates org binding on every deploy (small traffic to staging). previously the canary only checked latency and health.

ashok: thanks — looks like no customer data exfil confirmed so far, just unauthorized reads of policy objects. marking incident as "triage in-progress". will attach logs to the incident ticket.

jordan: please add a short summary to #incidents and tag legal if anything changes. good catch, ashok.

ashok: filed incident INC-2026-045, link https://incidents/internal/INC-2026-045

maria: done on mitigation and PR opened. will follow up in the PM with timelines. :lock:
